thread:
alice: FYI saw two OOMs on prod-gpu-07 during the 21:00 gen-test. Both correlate with a sudden batch-size spike and a kernel switch to kernel_fast_gemm. KV cache memory balloons and then the process gets killed.

ben: link to incident log: https://rwd-infer/issue/1289 — looks like a pageflip/alloc storm.

chen: I can repro locally with a long-context run (12k tokens) + bursty concurrent users. Minimal repro:```./run_infer --model redwood-v2 --batchers 32 --concurrency 48 --tokens 12000 --kernel-policy auto``` yields same mem growth.

alice: interesting: kernel switch happens when observed latency crosses 180ms (our heuristic), which increases per-kv-entry allocation size in the fast kernel path. That plus prefix reuse fills gaps -> fragmentation (slab holes) and then pageflip.

erika: can we gate kernel switches on kv_free_headroom > X? or prefer kernel_stable for long-context flows?

ben: short-term mitigation: lower max_batch_size to 48 for that model/pool and add a soft-throttle on bursty joins. Also add an alert for kv.pageflip_rate > 0.02/min.

chen: added a perf dump snippet from repro run:```heap_map: slab=0x7f9b3c000 size=64 free=12 used=52
slabhole: start=0x7f9b3c400 len=4096
kv_entry: 0x7f9b3c500 len=256 ref=3 kernel=fast_gemm``` shows many small free holes between large used ranges.

perf-bot: perf report uploaded to https://perf.rwd/33321 group: kernel_fast_gemm, top consumers: memcpy, kvmem_alloc, attention_kernel.

alice: proposed patch: during kernel selection, check: if (expected_kv_growth(sequence_len, batch) > free_headroom * 0.6) prefer stable kernel OR trigger kv_compact_on_alloc(true). Pushed to canary branch, 3345.

deploy-bot: deploy started for canary/eng-runtime 3345 -> prod-gpu-07 :rocket:

ben: longer-term: add a background kv-compactor that runs when pageflip_rate spikes, plus a spill-to-disk emergency path (experimental). Also we should make kernel selection cost-aware (bytes per token) not just latency.

chen: running compact experiment on canary now, will run overnight with synthetic long-context traffic and report back.

erika: I'll draft a short playbook: on OOMs look at kv.pageflip_rate, kernel switches, recent batcher config changes; immediate steps: reduce max_batch_size, force kernel=stable, restart worker if kv_compact fails.

alice: also adding a temporary metric kv.oom_retry_count and a fallback that retries request with kernel=stable + batch=1 up to 2 times before failing gracefully with partial output.

ben: note: this is different from previous slab-only OOMs — root cause seems to be kernel-induced per-entry growth combined with reuse pattern that creates fragmentation. We should tag perf regression 0.52.

chen: experiment results: compacting reduces slabholes by ~70% and prevents OOM under our synthetic burst. I pushed a small change to kv manager to prefer in-place reuse (kv_reuse_bias=0.8).

alice: great. Action items: chen -> run compact on prod canary and collect metrics; ben -> add alert+dashboard; erika -> playbook + runbook update; alice -> follow up tomorrow on whether to roll lower max_batch_size org-wide for that model.

erika: ack :white_check_mark:

ben: can we add a short note to eng-runtime channel so SRE knows to expect config flicker tonight?

alice: posted a heads-up in #eng-oncall. Closing this thread, reopen if we see more OOMs after canary. :slightly_smiling_face:
